metadata.note: The Nashville and Decatur's main line Nashville - Franklin - Columbia - Pulaski - Athens - Decatur, opened through on 22 Nov 1860 by three companies (Tennessee and Alabama; Central Southern; Tennessee and Alabama Central) running jointly as the "Nashville & Decatur Railroad Line", consolidated as the Nashville and Decatur Railroad on 21 Nov 1866, and operated by the Louisville and Nashville from 1 Jul 1872. It was the L&N's Nashville - Birmingham main line until July 1914, then a secondary line after through trains moved to the new Brentwood - Lewisburg - Athens line. Two features on identical geometry: N&D 1860-1862 and 1866-1872 (Civil War gap left empty), L&N 1872-1914 and 1914-1951 [OPEN].
metadata.ownership_split: 22 Nov 1860 three predecessors -> joint Nashville & Decatur Railroad Line: drawn as the start of the N&D feature, not a split (the predecessors are not drawn separately). 21 Nov 1866 consolidation: not a split. 1 Jul 1872 N&D -> L&N (ICC; Pulaski Citizen says 1871): the Rule 4 split between the two features. 1899/1900 999-year re-lease: not a split.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn: the predecessor companies' own-name service before 22 Nov 1860 (no confirmed own-name passenger year for most of the line; the T&A 1855 Franklin date conflicts with the ICC's 1859); 1862-1865 US Military Railroad operation; 15 Sep 1865 - 21 Nov 1866 civil operation (bracketed, not confirmed); the Columbia - Mount Pleasant stub (report block [7], drawable NONE before its 1883 sale; later part of florence_muscle_shoals_railroads.geojson); the 1914 Brentwood - Lewisburg - Athens line (block [9], belongs to the L&N Nashville - Montgomery feature); 1952-1954 on Nashville - Columbia (the 7 Dec 1954 Columbia marker is unverified).
metadata.freight_only_check: No freight-only years drawn. Brentwood - Columbia (CSX), Columbia - Pulaski (Tennessee Southern from 1 Feb 1989) and Pulaski - Athens (until lifted c.1969) carried freight after passenger service ended; none of it is drawn. The old Athens - M&C junction alignment was replaced in 1913, not freight-only.
metadata.horsecar_check: None: steam railroad from opening (Rule 5 not engaged).
conflicts: L&N takeover: ICC valuation 1 Jul 1872 vs Pulaski Citizen 1871 ("leased the line from Nashville to Decatur"; proposal reported 30 Mar 1871). A RootsWeb page citing Fairfax Harrison (1901) gives "30 years from July 1, 1872". 1872 used.

Predecessor openings: T&A Nashville - Franklin 1855 (Franklin marker, via search summary only) vs 1859 (ICC); Central Southern to Pulaski "June 30" in 1858, 1859 or 1860 (Pulaski Citizen extract without a clear year; ICC 1859; first locomotive 27 Apr 1860). Not drawn either way - the layer starts at the 22 Nov 1860 through opening.
Merger date: csa-railroads.com "did not become a single corporation until 1867" vs Pulaski Citizen 1866; reconciled by the ICC (organised 21 Nov 1866, Alabama act 8 Mar 1867).
not_yet_sourced: END OF PASSENGER SERVICE via Columbia/Pulaski is [OPEN] at 1951 (Feb 1952 Official Guide). Upper bound: a Columbia historical marker (hmdb m=151171, read only through search-result text; hmdb returns 403) says the last passenger train left Columbia's Union Station on 7 Dec 1954. That date is NOT drawn. Which trains ran 'via Columbia' in 1951, and when the last Pulaski/Athens train ran, are not established. Next sources: Pulaski Citizen / Columbia Daily Herald 1951-1955, ICC train-discontinuance dockets, L&N employee timetables, Fowler's branchline.uk Tennessee SL242 / Alabama SL244 files (unreachable during research).

Franklin, Tenn. appears in the Feb 1952 Official Guide index as "Louisville & Nashv. t" with no table number - 't' is how this OCR renders the freight-only dagger - which would mean no passenger stop at Franklin in 1951 while trains still ran via Columbia. Possibly a train not stopping, possibly OCR noise; unresolved. Pulaski, Lynnville and Tanner lost their table numbers in the OCR.

Table 30 (Nashville, Columbia and Florence, 1951) - rail or motor coach? Its OCR header carries 'Bus.' tokens with Table 27 interleaved. Bears on the Nashville - Columbia stretch after 1951 and on florence_muscle_shoals_railroads.geojson's 1948 end; not resolved and not used here.
Exact month through trains moved to the Lewisburg line: July 1914 from a railfan forum post only.
Exact month of the last civil N&D train in 1862, and whether civil trains ran between the 15 Sep 1865 return and the 21 Nov 1866 organisation.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; no timetable times were read for any year.

OPEN ISSUE IN ANOTHER LAYER (not edited here): ln_nashville_birmingham_montgomery.geojson draws its Nashville - Decatur leg as a single straight chord ([-86.7816, 36.1627] -> [-86.9878, 34.6059], c.108 mi) lying within c.8 km of Lewisburg - i.e. closer to the 1914 Lewisburg line than to this route - for one 1872-1971 segment with no split at 1914. For 1872-1914 the L&N's through trains ran over the line drawn in this layer (via Columbia and Pulaski), so that feature draws a later alignment for those years, its geometry_quality does not label the straight legs or their mileage (Rule 2), and the single segment hides the July 1914 re-routing. The fix belongs in that layer (split at 1914; draw 1872-1914 on this geometry or end it there).

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced end to end from OpenStreetMap, no straight-line legs: 120.8 mi drawn Nashville (Union Station) - Decatur against 119.3 mi documented (ICC valuation, 119.277 mi Nashville - Decatur Junction) and 122 mi (Central Southern annual report, 1 Oct 1861) - 1.3% over the ICC figure, 1.0% under 1861; the extra is mostly the last c.1.0 mi beyond Decatur Junction over the Southern (ex-Memphis and Charleston) Tennessee River bridge into Decatur, which the ICC figure stops short of. Routed with opstrace.py over OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=L&N (119.6 mi of the drawn line), plus 1.0 mi of the Southern bridge track and 0.3 mi untagged. By section (approx. mileposts from the waypoints): Nashville - Brentwood 0-9.5 on the live CSX ex-L&N main (Nashville Terminal Subdivision); Brentwood - Columbia 9.5-45.7 on live CSX/Tennessee Southern freight track; Columbia - Pulaski 45.7-79.2 on Tennessee Southern Railroad ways (no route relation; routed through); Pulaski - state line - Elkmont 79.2-98.8 LIFTED, traced on OSM abandoned-railway ways tagged old_railway_operator=L&N, many of them roads now built on the bed (Old Railroad Bed Road, Pulaski Highway, Old Elkton Pike and others) and the north end of the Richard Martin Trail; Elkmont - Athens 98.8-106.7 on the Richard Martin Trail rail-trail; Athens - Decatur 106.7-120.8 on live CSX. OpenHistoricalMap returned no railway ways for the Pulaski - Elkmont gap, so the lifted stretch rests on the OSM abandoned-bed tagging alone. Waypoints (Nominatim, every type checked: Nashville Union Station, Thompson's Station and the Decatur end hand-pinned because the geocoder returned a road and a city centroid; the rest are town/village/hamlet points, none a county) lie within 1.5 km of the line; Spring Hill (1.4 km), Decatur (1.2 km) and Pulaski (1.0 km) are town centroids off the track. The trace stays on the old route through Franklin, Columbia, Pulaski and Elkmont throughout; it does not touch the 1914 Brentwood - Lewisburg - Athens line. LATER ALIGNMENT: (1) Athens - Decatur (c.14.1 mi) is drawn on the L&N-built 1912-13 Athens - Decatur Junction line; the original 1860 alignment to the Memphis and Charleston junction near Decatur (c.12 mi, abandoned 1913) has no surviving OSM or OHM trace, so every pre-1913 year on this feature draws that stretch on the later route. (2) The Nashville end is drawn into the present CSX terminal trackage at Union Station (opened 1900), not the N&D's own 1860s Nashville depot, whose site is not located. Same geometry as the other feature in this layer (Rule 4 split at 1 Jul 1872).

segments.note: Through passenger trains Nashville - Brentwood - Franklin - Thompson's Station - Spring Hill - Columbia - Culleoka - Lynnville - Pulaski - Prospect - Elkmont - Athens - Decatur from 22 Nov 1860, the day after the Central Southern was completed to the Alabama line. These trains ran under the joint operating agreement of the three predecessor companies - the Tennessee and Alabama (Nashville - Columbia), the Central Southern (Columbia - state line) and the Tennessee and Alabama Central (state line - Decatur) - under the name "Nashville & Decatur Railroad Line", 122 miles, connecting at Decatur with the Memphis and Charleston (Central Southern annual report, 1 Oct 1861: "on the next day, November the 22d, the cars ran over the whole Line for the first time"). The predecessors' own-name trains before 22 Nov 1860 are not drawn: no own-name passenger year is confirmed for most of the line, and the 1855 Franklin date conflicts with the ICC's 1859 (see metadata). END 1862: Union forces occupied Nashville in Feb 1862 and the line passed to military use; the month of the last civil train is not established, so the earlier bracket year 1862 is drawn. The 1862-1865 US Military Railroad operation is deliberately NOT drawn (military operation, not company passenger service). Headway 720 min reflects the "double daily trains" of an 1861 notice cited by csa-railroads.com (not read at source); treat as an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start 22 Nov 1860 from the Central Southern's own annual report of 1 Oct 1861; the joint-line name and "double daily trains" from csa-railroads.com's N&D page and its 1861-62 documents list. The 1862 end is the Union occupation of Nashville (Feb 1862) - no source dates the last civil train.

segments.note: The Nashville and Decatur Railroad Company, organised 21 Nov 1866 (Tennessee act 19 Apr 1866, Alabama act 8 Mar 1867) by consolidating the three predecessors, ran Nashville - Decatur passenger trains until the L&N took over. The US Government returned the railroad to the company on 15 Sep 1865 (N&D stockholders' report, Pulaski Citizen 28 Nov 1867); the ICC says each predecessor was "operated by its own organization until November 21, 1866", so 1865-1866 civil operation is bracketed but not drawn - 1866 is the confirmed start. The Pulaski Citizen reports "an extra accommodation train will run from this place to Nashville daily" (23 Nov 1867) and an 1871 northbound passenger-train wreck. END 1872: L&N operation from 1 Jul 1872 per the ICC valuation. CONFLICT: the Pulaski Citizen says the L&N "leased the line from Nashville to Decatur" in 1871 (proposal reported 30 Mar 1871); the ICC date is the stronger source and is used - perhaps signed 1871, effective 1872. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE (two trains each way assumed from the 1860 pattern plus the 1867 extra accommodation train); not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: start (organised 21 Nov 1866) and end (L&N operation from 1 Jul 1872) from the ICC valuation; return of the line 15 Sep 1865, the 1867 accommodation train and the conflicting 1871 lease date from Pulaski Citizen extracts. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: L&N operation from 1 Jul 1872 (ICC valuation; Pulaski Citizen says the lease dates from 1871 - conflict recorded in metadata). The N&D gave the L&N its Nashville - Decatur link to the South and North Alabama, and this was the L&N's through Nashville - Decatur - Birmingham - Montgomery main line via Franklin, Columbia and Pulaski until July 1914, when the new Brentwood - Lewisburg - Athens line opened and through trains left this route. The 18 Oct 1899 999-year re-lease (from 1 Jul 1900) did not change the operator. END 1914: the switch to the Lewisburg line is dated July 1914 only by a railfan forum post; the ICC gives that line's construction as 1911-1914. Headway 480 min is an ESTIMATE for a main line carrying the Nashville - Montgomery through trains plus locals; no timetable was counted.
sources: Segment-level: start 1 Jul 1872 from the ICC valuation (lease conflict from Pulaski Citizen extracts); the 1914 end from the ICC's 1911-1914 construction dates for the Lewisburg line and a forum post for July 1914 (month NOT VERIFIED at a primary source). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Secondary line after July 1914: Nashville - Franklin - Columbia - Pulaski - Athens - Decatur local(s), the "via Columbia" trains, while the through trains used the Lewisburg line. Positive evidence for the last drawn year: the Feb 1952 Official Guide's L&N Nashville - Decatur table (Table 1) carries the footnote "Via Columbia", two of its train columns print that symbol instead of a time at Ardmore, and the index lists Prospect, Tenn. and Elkmont, Ala. - stations only on this old line - against Table 1 with no freight dagger. Times for those stations are not recoverable from the OCR. OPEN END: passenger service is confirmed to 1951 by that Guide. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no verified source dates when service actually stopped (a Columbia historical marker, read only via search summaries, gives a last train from Columbia on 7 Dec 1954; see not_yet_sourced). Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued after passengers ended (Brentwood - Columbia CSX; Columbia - Pulaski Tennessee Southern from 1989; Pulaski - Athens until the rails were lifted c.1969) - not drawn. Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE (one local each way assumed); not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: start from the July 1914 Lewisburg-line opening (ICC 1911-1914; July from a forum post, NOT VERIFIED); end 1951 [OPEN] from the Feb 1952 Official Guide OCR (Table 1 'Via Columbia' footnote and the Prospect and Elkmont index entries). Headway not sourced.
